name: Iron Lung
switches: KYBD on for VCO 1, 2 and 3; sync off; VCF mode 4072; envelope routing = keyboard/MIDI gate; ADSR time factor x1. VCO 3's normalled saw sits one octave under the other two. ADSR drives the VCA through its normalled exponential input; AR (VCA Env amount) stays at 0. (est.: all fader values)
play: Stab low notes (C1-C2) in tight 16ths for EBM lines. Pull decay toward 2 for a harder click, or raise resonance to about 5 for more bite.
adapt: The original was played from the 3620 keyboard; here the MIDI-to-CV feeds the VCOs. The saw outputs are patched in by hand because the VCF mixer is normalled to VCO 1 square and VCO 2 pulse.
sourceName: Built from: ARP 2600 Fundamentals manual (3-VCO bass)

name: Black Ice
switches: Extra: VCO 2 PWM amount = 3. VCO 3 in LF (low) mode with KYBD off (slow sweep, about one cycle every 2 s); VCO 1 and VCO 2 KYBD on, VCO 1 one octave under VCO 2 as a square sub. VCF mode 4012. VCA amplitude from the ADSR. (est.)
play: A slow, shifting pulse bass for darkwave and synthwave lines. Speed VCO 3 up for a nervous chorus effect, or slow it right down so each bar sounds slightly different.
adapt: The manual's PWM example used an audio VCO as the modulator; here VCO 3 in low mode acts as the LFO. Patching into the PWM jack replaces the noise normal.
sourceName: Built from: ARP 2600 Fundamentals manual (PWM)

name: Sync Grinder
switches: VCO 2 SYNC to VCO 1 on; KYBD on for VCO 1 and 2. VCO 1 is the silent sync master. VCF mode 4072. The ADSR also shapes the filter and VCA through its normals. (est.)
play: Every note opens with a tearing sync sweep that settles as the decay finishes, good for darksynth and EBM offbeat bass. More VCO 2 FM gives a nastier sweep; VCO 2 coarse changes the core vowel.
adapt: Uses the Behringer's VCO 2 sync-to-VCO 1 switch.
sourceName: Built from: hard sync (Behringer 2600 notes)

name: Growl Engine
switches: VCO 1 FM 2nd input = slider normalled to VCO 2 sine (VCO 2 is an unheard, slightly detuned modulator). VCF mod input 1 = slider normalled to VCO 2 sine. Three copies of VCO 1's saw hit the filter to drive it hard. VCF mode 4072 (24 dB). KYBD on for VCO 1 and 2. Noise colour white. (est.: fader values)
play: Thick, snarling bass for industrial and darksynth. The audio-rate FM pushes pitch up, so drop VCO 1 coarse until it sits in key, then use VCO 2 fine tune to set the growl speed.
adapt: Arturia's sequencer re-trigger trick is replaced by the normalled ADSR, and its global tune offset by lowering VCO 1 coarse. The Arturia-only delay and chorus are left out.
sourceName: Audiotent ARP 2600 bass tip

name: Basement 808
switches: VCO 2 KYBD on. The AR gives a quick pitch thump at the start of each note; the ADSR (exponential normal) sets the long boom. The VCA's AR slider (Env amount) is at 0 so the AR only bends pitch. VCF left open. (est.)
play: Long sub-boom for spooky lo-fi hip hop in the C1-C2 range. Push the VCO 2 mixer and VCA input into gentle overdrive, and lengthen decay for trap-style tails.
sourceName: Built from: SOS Synth Secrets (pitch-swept sine)

name: Rust Sync
switches: VCO 2 SYNC to VCO 1 on; VCO 1 and 2 KYBD on; VCO 3 in LF (low) mode, KYBD off, about 0.5 Hz. No portamento. VCF mode 4012. (est.)
play: A cutting darksynth lead whose sync tone slowly ramps and resets. Raise VCO 2 coarse for a brighter scream, or set VCO 3 faster for a ripping, sputtering texture.
adapt: Uses the Behringer's VCO 2 sync switch, with VCO 3 in low mode standing in for the 3620 keyboard LFO.
sourceName: Built from: hard sync (Behringer 2600 notes)

name: Devil's Interval
switches: All three VCOs KYBD on. Tune VCO 2 a tritone (6 semitones) above VCO 1 with the Toolkit tuner; VCO 3 one octave below VCO 1, very slightly sharp. VCF mode 4072. (est.: coarse values are starting points)
play: Every note plays a tritone chord: a menacing, horror-film lead. Swap the tritone for a minor sixth for a darker but less unstable colour.
sourceName: Built from: ARP 2600 Fundamentals manual (VCOs in intervals)

name: Rasp
switches: Extra: VCO 2 PWM amount = 4 (PWM jack left empty, so it stays normalled to noise). Noise colour white. VCO 1 and 2 KYBD on, VCO 1 one octave lower. VCF mode 4012. (est.)
play: Noise jitters the pulse width, so the lead sounds torn and breathy, like a worn tape. Turn PWM up for real grit or down for a cleaner, hollow tone.
sourceName: Built from: ARP 2600 Fundamentals manual (noise PWM)

name: Cold Glass
switches: Ring mod AUDIO coupling. VCO 1 and 2 KYBD on, VCO 2 at a non-harmonic interval (about a major ninth plus a few cents). VCF mode 4012. (est.)
play: A bell-like, unsettling lead whose overtones never resolve. Sweep VCO 2 fine tune while you play to bend it from glassy to clanging.
sourceName: Built from: JonDent ARP 2600 ring modulator

name: Ash Cathedral
switches: ADSR time factor x2. S&H samples its normalled noise on the internal clock; keep the S&H FM sliders on VCO 1 and VCO 2 at 0 so pitch stays steady. Envelope routing = keyboard/MIDI. VCF mode 4072. (est.)
play: Hold single notes or slow fifths. The lagged random voltage makes the filter wander, so every note breathes on its own. Try a slower S&H rate for longer drifts.
adapt: Monophonic like the original. For chords, layer recordings in Ableton.
sourceName: Built from: ARP 2600 Fundamentals manual (S&H + lag)

name: Reverse Bloom
switches: The inverted ADSR pulls the filter down while the key is held, then opens it as the note fades. The AR goes to the VCA exponential input (replacing the ADSR normal), with the VCA's AR slider (Env amount) at 0. KYBD on for VCO 1 and 2. VCF mode 4012. (est.)
play: Each note swells in dark, then brightens on release like tape played backwards. Leave space between notes so you hear the bloom.
sourceName: Built from: ARP 2600 Fundamentals manual (inverted envelope)

name: Static Veil
switches: Extra: VCO 2 PWM amount = 5. VCO 3 in LF (low) mode, KYBD off, very slow. Noise colour pink, as a quiet hiss layer. ADSR time factor x2. VCF mode 4072. (est.)
play: A hissy, slowly moving PWM wash for dark ambient beds. Raise the noise for a broken-radio feel, or close the filter to push it into the distance.
adapt: VCO 3 in low mode stands in for the PWM modulator; patching the PWM jack replaces the noise normal.
sourceName: Built from: ARP 2600 Fundamentals manual (PWM)

name: Abyss
switches: KYBD off on all three VCOs (fixed drone). VCO 1 and 2 nearly unison so they beat slowly; VCO 3 an octave up and slightly flat. Noise colour low (rumble). VCA initial gain holds it open with no keys. Keep the VCO S&H FM sliders at 0. VCF mode 4072. (est.)
play: Leave it running under a track and ride cutoff and resonance by hand. Retune VCO 3 to a minor second above VCO 1 for real dread.
sourceName: Built from: ARP 2600 Fundamentals manual (S&H + lag)

name: Power Station
switches: Ring mod AUDIO coupling, fed by its normalled VCO 1/VCO 2 inputs, both very low and slightly detuned. KYBD off on all VCOs; VCO 3 in LF (low) mode as a slow filter sweep. Noise colour low. VCA initial gain keeps it running. VCF mode 4012. (est.)
play: An industrial mains-hum and turbine drone. Nudge VCO 2 fine tune for faster beating and push resonance until the filter starts to whistle above the hum.
sourceName: Built from: JonDent ARP 2600 ring modulator

name: Filter Wraith
switches: No audio enters the filter; full resonance makes it ring on its own. VCF mod input 1 = slider normalled to VCO 2 sine (VCO 2 KYBD off, low audio rate), so the whine growls. VCF keyboard CV stays normalled, so keys transpose it. VCF mode 4012. (est.)
play: Ride the cutoff fader slowly for a haunted whistle. More VCO 2 mod gives snarling sidebands; at 0 it's a pure sine drone.
sourceName: Built from: ARP 2600 Fundamentals manual (self-oscillating VCF)

name: Swarm
switches: Cross-FM: VCO 3's saw drives VCO 2 (patched), and VCO 2's sine drives VCO 3 through VCO 3's normalled sine input (FM input 2). KYBD off on both. VCO 2 pulse and VCO 3 saw reach the filter through their normals. VCF mode 4072. (est.)
play: A chaotic, insect-like cloud that changes with tiny fader moves; small changes to either FM amount swing it from slow wobble to harsh noise.
sourceName: Built from: ARP 2600 Fundamentals manual (cross FM)

name: Pit Kick
switches: Self-oscillating filter kick: resonance full, cutoff at minimum, the ADSR sweeps the cutoff down and shapes the VCA (exponential normal). ADSR time factor x0.5 (est.). VCF mode 4012 or 4072; try both. All mixer inputs at 0.
play: Play C1-C2; the filter's keyboard tracking sets the pitch. Lower resonance slightly and add a little VCO 1 in the mixer for a click.
adapt: The source recipe is for the ARP Axxe (resonance max, cutoff min, env about 50%, decay and release about 50%, sustain 0). It maps one-to-one onto the 2600's faders, with the time factor switch added.
sourceName: SOS Synth Secrets: bass drum

name: Steel Kick
switches: Oscillator kick: a short ADSR drops VCO 2's pitch, and a longer AR sets the body (patched into the VCA exponential input, replacing the ADSR normal). VCO 2 KYBD on. Filter wide open, VCF Env amount 0. (est.)
play: A punchy, tunable industrial kick. A shorter ADSR decay gives a tighter click; more VCO 2 FM gives a bigger zap at the start.
sourceName: Built from: 'How to KickDrum with the Oscillator of Behringer ARP 2600' (YouTube)

name: Shell Snare
switches: VCO 2 FM input 2 = slider normalled to VCO 1 square. VCO 1 at a high audio rate frequency-modulates VCO 2's 25% pulse for the 'shell' tone. Noise colour white. No resonance (it would make the tail sing). VCA from the ADSR (exponential normal). KYBD on. (est.: VCO tunings)
play: Snare and noise layer in one for EBM and industrial backbeats. The pulse width and FM amount are touchy; nudge them until the body sounds like a drum, not a beep.
adapt: The source is an SH-101 recipe (noise 10, filter freq/env/kybd 10, res 0, A0 D2 S0 R2, 25% pulse). The 101's audio-rate LFO is replaced here by VCO 1 square through VCO 2's normalled FM input.
sourceName: SOS Synth Secrets: snare drum

name: Tin Hat
switches: Ring mod AUDIO coupling. VCO 1 and 2 tuned high and well apart (non-harmonic), KYBD off. Noise colour white. ADSR time factor x0.5. VCF mode 4012. (est.: tunings and cutoff)
play: A closed metallic hat. Raise decay and release to about 4 for an open hat or trashy ride. Small moves on either VCO coarse change the metal a lot.
adapt: The source uses an MS-20 with high-pass and band-pass filters. The 2600 only has a low-pass, so resonance near the top stands in for the narrow high band.
sourceName: SOS Synth Secrets: cymbals

name: Ritual Tom
switches: A short noise burst pings a highly resonant filter, which rings at the played pitch (VCF keyboard CV normalled). Noise colour white. VCA from the ADSR (exponential normal). VCF mode 4072. (est.)
play: Play toms across an octave (C2-C3) for tribal fills. Raise resonance toward 9.5 for a longer, more tuned ring.
sourceName: Built from: ARP 2600 owner's manual (noise through resonant VCF)

name: Steel Drum Ghost
switches: Each key press takes a new noise sample, so the filter lands somewhere slightly different on every hit. Keep the S&H FM sliders on VCO 1 and 2 at 0. VCO 1 at an inharmonic ratio above VCO 2 to feed the ring mod (normalled inputs). KYBD on for both. (est.: all values)
play: Tuned metallic hand percussion, somewhere between bongo and steel drum. Higher resonance and release make it more steel; less makes it more bongo.
sourceName: Eevo Lute: B2600 patching ep. 2

name: Night Wind
switches: Noise colour between white and pink. S&H samples noise on the internal clock; heavy lag turns the steps into gusts. VCA held open by initial gain (no keys needed). VCF mode 4012. (est.)
play: Howling, irregular wind for intros and dark ambient. Push resonance toward 8 for whistling through cracks; vary the S&H rate to change how gusty it is.
sourceName: Built from: NewMusicBox environmental sounds

name: Black Surf
switches: VCO 3 in LF (low) mode, KYBD off, about one cycle every 6-8 s. The inverted, lagged ramp gives each wave a fast crash and a slow pull-back, opening both filter and VCA. VCA Env amount = the slider on the linear CV jack now carrying the wave. Noise colour pink to low. (est.)
play: A cold, endless shoreline. Slow VCO 3 for bigger swells; a little more resonance adds hissy spray on each crash.
sourceName: Built from: NewMusicBox environmental sounds

name: Air Raid
switches: VCO 3 in LF (low) mode, KYBD off. Its square through the lag becomes a rise-and-fall curve that sweeps VCO 1's pitch like a wartime siren. VCO 1 KYBD off. VCA held open by initial gain. (est.)
play: Ride VCO 3 coarse for the wail speed and lag time for how swoopy it is. Drop initial gain to 0 to play it from the keys with the ADSR instead.
sourceName: Built from: ARP 2600 Fundamentals manual (lag processor)

name: Laser Bolt
switches: A large ADSR amount on VCO 1's pitch gives a fast downward 'pew'. VCO 1 KYBD on. VCA from the ADSR (exponential normal). ADSR time factor x0.5 for tight zaps, x2 for falling bombs. (est.)
play: Short taps for blasters, longer holds for dive-bombs. Turn VCO 2 sync on and mix VCO 2 in for a harsher, torn laser.
sourceName: Built from: ARP 2600 Fundamentals manual (envelope as FM source)

name: Droid Chatter
switches: Envelope routing switch set to S/H CLOCK, so every clock tick fires a blip. VCO 1's KYBD/CV FM slider now gets a lagged copy of the S&H (chirpy glides, fine for FX); VCO 2 gets the raw S&H through its normal. Ring mod uses its normalled VCOs. (est.)
play: Fast, chirping robot babble. Change the S&H rate for nervous or relaxed chatter; press MANUAL or set routing back to keyboard for single phrases.
sourceName: Built from: ARP 2600 droid-voice history + S&H

name: Robot Mouth
switches: Extra: Preamp gain = 7 (mic or line into the preamp, which is also normalled to the envelope follower). Extra: VCA ring-mod input slider = 0. The follower drives the VCA exponential input (replacing the ADSR normal), so keys only set VCO 1's pitch. Ring mod AUDIO coupling. VCO 1 KYBD on. Noise colour white. (est.)
play: Speak or sing into the preamp while holding a note: your voice gets ring-modulated by the saw and gated by its own loudness for a cold robot voice. Change notes for pitch; a little more noise makes consonants clearer.
adapt: Needs a mic or line source into the Behringer's preamp input.
sourceName: Built from: ARP 2600 Fundamentals manual (preamp, follower, ring mod)

name: Anvil
switches: Ring mod (AUDIO coupling) uses its normalled VCO 1 and VCO 2 inputs at a non-harmonic ratio. VCO 3's saw adds a third, unrelated partial. KYBD on for all three, so the clang tracks the keys. VCF mode 4012. (est.)
play: Factory hits, chains and struck metal for industrial tracks. Different VCO 2/3 tunings give a different 'object'; a longer release in the reverb makes a cathedral bell.
sourceName: Built from: ARP 2600 owner's manual (ring mod metallic tones)

name: Ghost Sweep
switches: VCO 1 holds a fixed pitch (KYBD off) while VCO 3 in LF (low) mode (KYBD off) slowly ramps VCO 2 upward; both feed the ring mod through its normals (AUDIO coupling). VCA held open by initial gain. (est.)
play: Spectral ghost tones rising and falling, with sum and difference partials sliding in opposite directions. Very slow VCO 3 settings work best for horror beds.
sourceName: Built from: ARP 2600 owner's manual (ring mod sweep)

name: Sentinel
switches: The classic random-pitch patch with no cables. S&H samples its normalled noise; VCO 1's KYBD/CV FM slider is normalled to the S&H output. Envelope routing switch = S/H CLOCK, so each new step re-fires the ADSR. VCO 1 KYBD on (keys transpose). VCF mode 4012. (est.)
play: The 'computer thinking' burble. Sync the clock to your track by ear, lower the FM amount for a narrower note range, raise resonance for squelchy bleeps.
sourceName: ARP 2600 owner's manual (S&H on noise)

name: Staircase
switches: VCO 3 in LF (low) mode, KYBD off. The S&H samples its slow ramp, so pitches climb in steps and reset. The S&H output reaches VCO 1 (KYBD/CV slider) and VCO 2 (input 1) through the normals. VCO 2 about a fifth above VCO 1. Envelope routing = S/H CLOCK. (est.)
play: Repeating up-staircase runs. Nudge VCO 3 coarse against the clock rate to change the pattern length; small FM amounts give near-chromatic runs, larger ones leaping patterns.
sourceName: ARP 2600 owner's manual (S&H sampling VCO 3 saw)

name: Stepped Filter Gate
switches: VCO 3 in LF (low) mode, KYBD off, as the sampled ramp. The S&H goes to the filter; the S&H FM sliders on VCO 1/2 stay at 0. Envelope routing = S/H CLOCK for a gated rhythm, or keyboard for held, stepping notes. VCO 1 and 2 KYBD on. VCF mode 4072. (est.)
play: Hold a bass note and the filter steps through a repeating pattern: a ready-made EBM sequence. Push resonance for acid squelch.
adapt: The manual sampled VCO 1 in LF mode; here VCO 3 (low) is the sampled ramp so VCO 1 and 2 stay audible.
sourceName: ARP 2600 owner's manual (S&H on filter)

name: Analog Bitcrush
switches: VCO 3 at audio rate (KYBD off) clocks the S&H, which resamples VCO 1's saw into aliased, decimated audio. Keep the S&H FM sliders on VCO 1/2 at 0 so the crushed audio doesn't leak into pitch. VCO 1 KYBD on. Envelope routing = keyboard. (est.)
play: Lo-fi, crunchy leads and basses. Lower VCO 3 coarse for heavier crushing, raise it for subtle grit; VCO 3 KYBD on makes the crush follow the notes.
sourceName: loopop 2600M patch ideas (analog bitcrush)

name: P.Y.T. Bounce
switches: Only VCO 2 (pulse) and VCO 3 (saw) are heard, both through their normals. VCO 2 and 3 KYBD on, VCO 3 a hair sharp. VCF mode 4012. VCA from the ADSR. (est.: values; only the VCO 2 + VCO 3 combination is documented)
play: A tight, bouncy two-oscillator bass in the spirit of the 'P.Y.T.' line. Play short syncopated notes; close the cutoff with more env amount for a darker, funkier pluck.
adapt: The original was played on an ARP 2600 with the 3620 keyboard; here the VCOs are driven over MIDI.
sourceName: MusicRadar: P.Y.T. ARP 2600 bass

name: Glass Bell
switches: Double FM: VCO 1 square (patched, replacing the noise normal on input 1) and VCO 2 sine (normalled, input 2) both modulate VCO 3, the only one heard. All three KYBD on so the ratios stay fixed across the keyboard. (est.)
play: Cold, bell-like FM tones for spooky melodies and music-box hooks. Detuning VCO 1 or 2 slightly moves the bell from pure to rotten.
sourceName: Built from: ARP 2600 Fundamentals manual (double FM)

name: Berlin Pulse
switches: VCO 1 at 16', VCO 2 one octave lower (32'), both slightly detuned. VCO 2 FM input 2 = slider normalled to VCO 1 square (gentle FM). Cutoff around 1 kHz with a little resonance. VCF mode 4072. KYBD on for VCO 1/2. (est.: fader positions for the stated values)
play: A sequenced saw pulse in the Berlin-school style. Drive it from Ableton, the MPC or the SQ-1 in 16ths and ride the cutoff for build-ups.
adapt: The 1601 sequencer, unison detune, chorus and delay from the source aren't on the Behringer: sequence over MIDI and add chorus and delay in Ableton.
sourceName: Audiotent: ARP 2600 sequence
